text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 27 in history.
1505 - Ivan III, Tsar of Russia, died. Known as Ivan the Great, he became tsar in 1462 and strengthened the authority of the monarchy and laid the foundations for a centralised state.
1553 - Michael Servetus (Miguel Serveto), Spanish physician and theologian whose teachings led to his being convicted of heresy and blasphemy and being burned at the stake.
1644 - The battle of Newbury took place when 9,000 Royalists under English King Charles I held out against the Parliamentary army of 17,500.
1662 - Charles II of England sold Dunkirk to France for 2-1/2 million Livres (400,000 pounds sterling).
1728 - James Cook born. British explorer and one of the great navigators in history. He mapped New Zealand, Australia and the Hawaiian Islands.
1782 - Niccolo Paganini born. Italian composer and virtuoso violinist whose own works reflected his extraordinary technique.

1795 - Pinckney's Treaty (also known as the Treaty of San Lorenzo) between Spain and the United States was signed. It established the former southern boundary of the United States at the 31st parallel and gave Americans the right to send goods down the Mississippi without paying duty to Spain.
1807 - The Treaty of Fontainebleau was signed by Napoleon of France and Charles IV of Spain which provided for the division of Portugal into three parts.
1811 - Isaac Singer born. U.S. inventor and manufacturer who developed the first practical sewing machine.

1858 - Theodore Roosevelt, U.S. president, writer, explorer and soldier born. He became governor of New York and then vice-president. He took over the presidency when William McKinley was assassinated in 1901 and served until 1909.
1871 - The diamond fields of Kimberley, South Africa, were annexed by Britain.
1914 - Dylan (Marlais) Thomas, Welsh poet and author born. Best known for "Under Milk Wood" a radio drama first broadcast posthumously in 1954.
1971 - The government of Congo announced that the country would change its name to the Republic of Zaire.
1978 - It was announced in Oslo that Menachem Begin of Israel and Anwar Sadat of Egypt had won the 1978 Nobel Peace Prize for their efforts towards peace in the Middle East.
1979 - St Vincent and the Grenadines became independent from Britain.
1986 - The "Big Bang" took place on the London Stock Exchange with the introduction of computerised dealing and deregulation of many controls.
1990 - New Zealand's voters ousted the Labour Party of Mike Moore giving the National Party under James Bolger the biggest election victory in more than 50 years.
1990 - Bandleader Xavier Cugat, the "Rumba King" of the 1930s and 40s who played a major role in popularising Latin American music died aged 90.
1991 - Turkmenistan's Supreme Soviet passed a law establishing its independence from the Soviet Union.
1995 - France set off the third in a series of nuclear tests in the south Pacific at Mururoa atoll.
1995 - A court in Milan sentenced two former Italian prime ministers, Bettino Craxi and Arnaldo Forlani to jail terms on corruption charges.
